headline: China's Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, 2.8T-param model
summary: Kimi K3 is the largest open-source AI model globally, rivaling top U.S. systems.
details: Moonshot AI, a Beijing-based startup backed by Alibaba, has released Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter model. It's now the largest open-source AI model globally, performing neck-and-neck with top proprietary systems from Anthropic and OpenAI.

The model features a 1-million-token context window, native visual understanding capabilities, and an always-on reasoning mode called 'thinking mode.' It's built on two key architectural innovations: Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals.

Kimi K3 is compatible with the OpenAI SDK, priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. A promotional top-up rebate offers up to 30% back in vouchers for API credits of $1,000 or more.
Benchmark results show Kimi K3 scoring 1,687 on GDPval-AA v2, 1,527 on AA-Briefcase, and 91.2 out of 100 on BrowseComp. It ranked first in four out of eight benchmarks for real-world task automation.
caption:

Kimi K3 is compatible with the OpenAI SDK, priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. A promotional top-up rebate offers up to 30% back in vouchers for API credits of $1,000 or more.

Benchmark results show Kimi K3 scoring 1,687 on GDPval-AA v2, 1,527 on AA-Briefcase, and 91.2 out of 100 on BrowseComp. It ranked first in four out of eight benchmarks for real-world task automation.

headline_marked: Roblox introduces [[AI-powered game creation]] on mobile
headline: Roblox introduces AI-powered game creation on mobile
summary: Roblox's new 'Build' feature lets users create games from text prompts. The feature will enter public alpha testing on July 28.
details: Roblox has announced a new feature called 'Build' that allows users to design games from their mobile devices using AI. The feature lets anyone turn simple text prompts into a basic game without any programming experience.

The Build feature is powered by a broad set of AI models, including both open-source and proprietary Roblox models. It handles gameplay mechanics, environment, characters, visual style, sound, and more.

The feature will enter public alpha testing on July 28, available to users in New Zealand aged nine and older who have verified their age. Users aged 16 and up will have the opportunity to publish their creations to a global audience.
Roblox plans to rank these AI-generated games based on player retention, similar to the system used for other games on the platform. If a game is not played, it won't be featured as prominently.
